wholeBodyReview.heading: Recognize the patient who needs support
wholeBodyReview.body: Assess nutrition support when safe oral intake cannot meet the patient’s needs. Relevant settings include dysphagia associated with neurologic disease or cancer treatment, critical illness, and requirements that cannot be met orally. These settings prompt assessment rather than establish an indication by diagnosis alone. Confirm that the proposed route can safely deliver nutrients to a functioning gastrointestinal tract. Selected patients with gastric outlet obstruction may be candidates for feeding beyond the obstruction when the small bowel is usable; complete intestinal obstruction requires withholding enteral feeding and clinical assessment. Match initiation to nutrition risk, anticipated intake, perfusion, and tolerance. Expected duration also guides access selection. A diagnosis or fixed day count alone does not establish a feeding indication.

metadataStatementReview.old: Detect intolerance, refeeding risk, aspiration, contamination, and mechanical complications early.
metadataStatementReview.new: Recognize signs that warrant assessment for intolerance, refeeding risk, aspiration, contamination, or mechanical complications.
metadataStatementReview.reason: Avoid promising early detection; describe recognition and assessment.

metadataStatementReview.old: Choose the least complex formula that meets nutrient, volume, digestion, absorption, electrolyte, and tolerance needs.
metadataStatementReview.new: Match formula composition to nutrient, volume, digestion, absorption, electrolyte, and tolerance needs; greater complexity does not establish greater benefit.
metadataStatementReview.reason: Match patient physiology and nutrient prescription; avoid a complexity-only rule.

metadataStatementReview.new: Calculate formula water from product composition and the volume actually delivered.
metadataStatementReview.reason: Water delivery depends on composition and actual volume; caloric density alone is not the calculation.

metadataStatementReview.old: When a problem appears, identify whether it is gastrointestinal, metabolic, mechanical, medication related, or infectious before changing the formula.
metadataStatementReview.new: When a problem appears, assess gastrointestinal, metabolic, mechanical, medication-related, and infectious causes. Respond promptly to urgent findings and reassess the feeding plan.
metadataStatementReview.reason: Do not imply urgent response must wait for a definitive causal category.
